svg.title: Level positions on the HMC table for levelling and twist
svg.text: Level positions on the HMC 500 bed (top view, 1:25) – the app model: 6 bolts, 4 reading positions
Tf / Tm / Tr = table front / middle / rear (X + Z level), C = column base (X only)
■ main bolt □ auxiliary bolt · forces = level state, CoG 0.3 m behind the centre
X reading = slope dw/dx: + means the RIGHT side is high → raise the left
Z reading = slope dw/dz: + means the REAR is high → raise the front
1 division of the precision level = 0.02 mm/m = 4.1 arc-seconds
Reversal: read r₁, turn the level 180° on the same spot, read r₂
(signed as slope): slope = (r₁ − r₂)/2, level zero error = (r₁ + r₂)/2
example r₁ = +0.03, r₂ = −0.01 → slope 0.02, level error 0.01 mm/m
How one move changes the readings (app model, from the level state, mm/m)
Front pair +1/32 (0.047 mm): a rigid bed would tilt 0.047/3.4 = 0.0138 mm/m; the middle
bolts make the bed bow, so the table reads 0.0211 – this is why aux bolts are set LAST.
twist = max(X_Tf, X_Tm, X_Tr, X_C) − min(X_Tf, X_Tm, X_Tr, X_C) ≤ 0.02 mm/m
If X changes from the table to the column, the bed is warped (wound).
Correct with ONE diagonal pair (1 + 6 or 2 + 5), small steps (1/32),
then read all four positions again. Never correct twist with aux bolts.
Order of work (app hint logic: loose bolt → height → Z → X → twist → aux bolts)
Tolerances (example – the maker decides): every reading ≤ 0.02 mm/m, twist ≤ 0.02 mm/m,
transfer height ±0.5 mm, every bolt ≥ 25 % of the average load (5.1 kN).
Level positions for levelling + twist – HMC 500
EXAMPLE – check the maker's installation manual
